scope: Current packed-entry opt-in native protected32 path, complete lean stock xv6 forktest; one unprofiled control and one low-rate V8 CPU profile; no emulator implementation change or speed claim

host.cpu: Intel Xeon Processor (Skylake, IBRS, no TSX), KVM, 4 vCPU
host.sharedHostLoadNote: One-minute load average was 6.95 on four vCPUs shortly after the two runs. User CPU seconds are recorded only as diagnostic context; one profile/control pair does not establish a speed effect.

reproduction.environment: XV6_LEAN=1 XV6_RAM_HASH=1 XV6_NATIVE_DISPATCH=1 XV6_FIRMWARE=bochs XV6_STEPS=40000000 XV6_STOP_ON_EXPECT=1 XV6_COMMAND=$'forktest\r' XV6_EXPECT_SERIAL=$'fork test OK\n$ '
reproduction.time: /usr/bin/time -f 'user=%U system=%S elapsed=%e maxrss_kb=%M' -o FILE before each env-prefixed node command
reproduction.profileDirectoryRequirement: Use an empty profile directory so the glob selects exactly one file.

profile.denominator: 4381 disjoint V8 self samples from the profiled whole Node process; no fallback observer or other diagnostic hook was enabled

interpretation: Ordinary JavaScript 386 fallback execution is the largest observed named category, even after packed native entry. Its 2051 samples are an attribution bucket, not a removable cost estimate. The 930 dispatcher/runner samples are a mixed envelope containing validation, admission, state transfer and decisions; V8 inlining can move helper costs into these frames. The direct fetch/decode bin is an overlap-safe lower bound for those named functions, not a hard ceiling on a future cache. Probe-script, GC and other host-runtime samples remain in the whole-process denominator but are not attributed to an emulator optimization. The profiled run paid profiler overhead and is not compared to the control as an A/B speed result.

candidateGate.candidate: Before coding an all-current-opcode, page-safe JavaScript fallback fetch/decode cache, require source-position or form-linked evidence that its actually affected non-overlapping path accounts for at least 15% of current packed-entry whole-process V8 self samples. Do not count all of _stepInstruction, step, translation or the mixed native entry frames as removable fetch/decode cost.
candidateGate.currentDirectFunctionEvidence: The named _decodeEA, _fetchN and _fetch8 functions contribute only 241/4381 = 5.50% direct self samples; this does not clear the 15% screening gate. Inlining prevents treating 5.50% as a definitive maximum, so a separate overlap-safe attribution is required before reconsidering the candidate.
candidateGate.retentionIfScreenLaterPasses: Require focused code-write/DMA, page-remap, A20, privilege, fault rollback and chip/LAPIC/IRQ differential tests; byte-identical complete xv6 report and RAM hash; then three serial adjacent unprofiled baseline/candidate user-CPU pairs with at least 5% lower mean and all three pairs favorable. Measure protected16/Windows effect separately before any general 386 claim.

priorNegativeComparison.movLeaInline: Duplicated 8B/8D effective-address decoding averaged 1.3% improvement over two pairs with a reversed pair; discarded in 2026-09-27-i80386-mov-lea-fastpath-negative.json.
priorNegativeComparison.registerTemplate: Cached 89/39/85 register templates averaged about 2.4% improvement, below its 10% gate; discarded in 2026-09-27-i80386-discarded-reg-cache.json.
priorNegativeComparison.nativeMemoryBranchCoverage: Page-safe 89/A4 and near-Jcc native coverage added 579024 retirements but delivered 0.22% mean user-CPU reduction with one reversed pair; discarded in 2026-09-28-i80386-native-coverage-no-go.json.
priorNegativeComparison.registerOnlyTrace: The current-source completed native-successor census found only 557642 optimistic register-only successor calls, below its 1.5M gate; see 2026-09-28-i80386-native-successor-census.json.

decision: No new production optimization is justified by this profile alone. A larger gain needs an architectural path that replaces enough fallback work per entry, with fault/event/code-write contracts and a measured overlap-safe opportunity count.
